title: Bucketed cost sensitivity and qpolicy recommendations
content:
Purpose:
This note consolidates a compact, spreadsheet-driven approach to generating bucketed cost / SLO tradeoffs and concrete qpolicy (quantization + batching + cache) suggestions for three traffic archetypes: low-latency conversational, high-throughput embedding, and mixed-session chat. The goal is a reproducible worksheet that product, solutions, and runtime can use to produce a recommended config per customer cohort.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Produce 3 traffic buckets by median request length and SLA: interactive-short (<=40 tokens, 50–200ms target), mixed-dialogue (avg 200 tokens, 300–800ms target), bulk-embed (500+ tokens or batch embeddings).
- For each bucket we recommend an initial qpolicy that balances cost vs quality: nf4 quantization for interactive with aggressive batching windows, q4_k_m for embed-heavy customers where minimal quality loss is acceptable, and hybrid (nf4 + lite prefix cache) for mixed.
- Spreadsheet model supports sensitivity sweeps on: model choice, qconfig, batch_size, batching-window-ms, prefix-kv-ttl, cold_start_rate. Output: estimated $/1M tokens, p50/p95 latency, and expected top-1 quality delta vs baseline fp16.

High-level recommendations (config snippets):
1) Interactive-short (bucket A)
   - model: redwood-ossa-7b-8k (or equivalent low-latency variant)
   - quant: nf4 (default) with outlier detection -> fall back to fp16 for hallucination triggers
   - batching: dynamic batching window = 6ms, max batch size = 8 requests/GPU
   - token-batching: prefer request-level batching (concatenate when from same session), target tokens-per-batch ~128
   - qcache: prefix cache TTL = 120s, max cached-prefix-tokens = 256
   - expected unit economics (spreadsheet example): $/1M tokens ≈ $28–$34 (range driven by cold start rate and p95 tail)

2) Mixed-dialogue (bucket B)
   - model: redwood-ossa-13b-8k
   - quant: nf4 for forward, allow q4_k_m for customers who sign off on 1–2% top-1 quality drop
   - batching: window = 12ms, max batch = 16, prefer KV-cache pinning for active sessions
   - qcache: session-aware KV cache, TTL = 900s, auto-evict least-recently-used sessions when memory > 75%
   - expected $/1M tokens ≈ $15–$22 depending on quant mix and cache hit rate

3) Bulk-embed / throughput-first (bucket C)
   - model: embed-rt-large or redwood-embed-2
   - quant: q4_k_m aggressively, consider 3-bit experimental profiles for cheap experiments (must be gated)
   - batching: large micro-batches, max batch size = 256 requests/GPU or tokens-per-batch target 32k, batching window = 50–120ms
   - qcache: NO prefix caching (not helpful for one-off embeddings), rely on token-level microbatch caching only
   - expected $/1M tokens ≈ $5–$9 with q4_k_m and sustained full GPU utilization

Spreadsheet walkthrough (columns / formulas):
- Columns: bucket, model, qconfig, batch_window_ms, max_batch, avg_request_tokens, avg_response_tokens, tokens_per_minute, cache_hit_rate, cold_start_pct, p50_ms, p95_ms, unit_cost_per_gpu_hr, tokens_per_gpu_hr, estimated_$per_1M_tokens, quality_delta_pct
- Key formulas (text form):
  - tokens_per_gpu_hr = (tokens_per_minute * 60) * gpu_efficiency_factor (0.7 baseline)
  - estimated_$per_1M_tokens = (unit_cost_per_gpu_hr / tokens_per_gpu_hr) * 1_000_000 * (1 + overhead_factor)
  - overhead_factor = (1 - cache_hit_rate) * cold_start_penalty_factor + batch_padding_waste
  - batch_padding_waste approximated as (avg_batch_fill_fraction_loss) e.g., (1 - avg_tokens_in_batch / max_tokens_in_batch)
- Sensitivity sweep tabs: vary cache_hit_rate 0–80%, cold_start_pct 0–15%, batching_window 2–120ms, and quant mix (fp16, nf4, q4_k_m). Output is a heatmap of $/1M tokens and p95 latency bucket.

Sample cell examples (to paste into spreadsheet):
- tokens_per_gpu_hr: = (G2*60)*0.7  where G2 is tokens_per_minute
- estimated_$per_1M_tokens: = (H2 / I2)*1000000*(1+J2)  -> H2 unit_cost_per_gpu_hr, I2 tokens_per_gpu_hr, J2 overhead_factor
Quality vs cost heuristics (short):
- nf4 generally preserves quality for conversational generation but can slightly degrade factuality; introduce a small eval harness per-customer (10–20 prompt pairs) to reject nf4 if >2% regression on correctness metrics
- q4_k_m reduces memory and increases throughput but may drop top-1 accuracy on long-context reasoning; only recommended for embed or retrieval-augmented single-shot tasks
- hybrid fallback: serve nf4 by default and on any model-specified "quality-fidelity trigger" route to fp16; implement routing cost delta attribution in billing sheet

Operational suggestions (rollout + telemetry):
- For new customers: run the spreadsheet-driven profiling runbook (linked spreadsheet) with sample traffic for 48–72 hours to estimate real cache_hit_rate and cold_start_pct.
- Canary: expose qpolicy per-route in console. Start with 5% traffic -> monitor quality evals, p95, and cost. Incrementally increase to 50% then 100% if quality deltas <1.5%.
- Alerts: auto-alert if p95 > SLO or if eval-quality delta > threshold. Fail open to fp16 for any live regression for 30 minutes.

Runbook checklist (for Solutions/SEs):
- [ ] Provision sample workload in sandbox cluster and run the spreadsheet (tab: "run-1")
- [ ] Collect: tokens/min, avg tokens/request, cold_start_rate, p50/p95 latencies, GPU utilization
- [ ] Fill bucket assignment columns and run sensitivity sweep (tab: "sensitivity")
- [ ] Decide initial qpolicy and set canary 5% with auto-fallback enabled
- [ ] Create ticket to instrument eval harness (INF-842) and attach results to customer folder

Unresolved / discussion items (for product & runtime):
- How to represent mixed quantization in the cost model cleanly (per-token weighting vs per-request)? Current spreadsheet uses request-weighted average of tokens but that underestimates context-reuse benefits. Need a better per-prefix amortization term.
- Should we expose a single toggle in Console ("economy / balanced / fidelity") mapping to these qpolicy presets or allow full low-level knobs? Preferences from sales suggest 80% of customers want presets.
- We need a small lab experiment to quantify NF4 hallucination risk for long-context RAG flows (proposal: 2k prompts across 10 datasets). Open question: acceptable failure-rate threshold.

Appendix: quick sensitivity example (numbers)
- Baseline: redwood-ossa-13b-8k, fp16, no cache, tokens_per_minute = 60k, unit_cost_per_gpu_hr = $3.5, gpu_efficiency = 0.7
  - tokens_per_gpu_hr = (60k*60)*0.7 = 2.52M tokens/hr
  - estimated_$per_1M_tokens = (3.5 / 2.52)*1M ≈ $1.39 per 1M tokens baseline (note: this is internal, multiply by markup for customer pricing)
- With nf4 + caching (cache_hit_rate = 40%, cold_start_pct = 3%, overhead=0.08) -> effective tokens_per_gpu_hr increases ~1.6x -> est $/1M_tokens falls to ~$0.85 (relative numbers used for internal decisioning)

Next steps (concrete):
1) Diego to add per-prefix amortization column to the spreadsheet and update the sensitivity tab (due: 2025-11-12)
2) Priya to draft short Console UX copy for three presets and example tooltips (due: 2025-11-14)
3) Run 48h profiling sandbox job for 5 pilot customers; collect cold_start_pct and cache_hit_rate (owner: Lucas; due: 2025-11-22)

Notes to self / draft markers: contains shorthand formulas and quick wins. This is intentionally compact — expansion to a full playbook (with step-by-step screenshots and sample dataset) is the next deliverable if the team prefers a customer-facing guide.

Relevant links and tickets: INF-842 (quantization-catalog), spreadsheet runbook: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AbCdEfGHij_kexample (tab: "sensitivity"), runtime PR for batching-window default: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/712

Prepared by: Ava Chen (product-optimize)
Reviewers: Diego Martinez, Priya Nair, Lucas Thompson

Open questions to discuss in 2025-11-19 sync:
- Should batch_window defaults be 6/12/60 ms for the three buckets? (vote in doc comments)
- What is the acceptance threshold on per-customer eval to auto-promote qpolicy from canary to full?

End of memo.
